The idea, known as a seed library, has since spread to more than forty towns in the region.

B  The founder, retired botanist Dr Mara Ellison, says the project began as a response to a loss she had noticed over several decades. For most of history, streets were simply dark after sunset. In the fifteenth century, some European cities introduced rules requiring householders to hang a lantern outside their door after dark. Not everyone obeyed, of course, and the light from a single candle didn't reach far.

Electric light arrived towards the end of the century. The first electric street lamps produced light from an arc between two carbon rods. The light was intensely bright – far too bright, in fact, for narrow streets, where it dazzled people rather than helping them.
